info.title: api4webtrees
info.description: JSON API for webtrees 2.2. Generated by tests/manifest.py from real responses – do not edit by hand.

get.summary: Entry point: versions, API level, signed-in user, the trees this user can see (with role and rights), CSRF token for POST requests and the largest accepted upload.
get.description: Entry point: versions, API level, signed-in user, the trees this user can see (with role and rights), CSRF token for POST requests and the largest accepted upload. From level 26 also `loginForm`, the settings of the sign-in page: `welcomeMessage`, `isSelfRegistrationAllowed` and `registrationTerms` (`null` when the site shows no terms). `welcomeMessage` and `registrationTerms` are HTML written by the site administrator, in the language of the request – show them as HTML only after sanitising. From level 31 each tree also has `availableModules`: the names of the enabled modules this user can use there (modules with an access level – menus, tabs, footers … – only when it allows the user), so a client can offer e.g. the privacy policy only when that module is on. This makes `Info` longer by one list of module names per tree. From level 37 every fact has `details`: the sub-structures without a field of their own (age, cause, phone, e-mail, pedigree, transliterations …) as rows `{tag, label, value, level}`, with label and value as webtrees shows them in the language of the request – a client can show any of them without reading GEDCOM. `sortName` shows unknown names as `…` instead of `@N.N.`/`@P.N.`.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

get.summary: List of individuals, sorted by name, 50 per page.
get.description: List of individuals, sorted by name, 50 per page. `q` filters by name; with `scope=all` the words may appear anywhere in the visible data (place, year, occupation …).

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

get.summary: One individual with facts, parent/spouse/step families, media and – with `relativeTo` – the relationship to another individual.
get.description: One individual with facts, parent/spouse/step families, media and – with `relativeTo` – the relationship to another individual. From level 28 each fact has `pending` (`true`: a change waiting for approval, visible only to users whom webtrees shows pending changes, i.e. editors and moderators) and `sex` is the value the user sees in the facts, also while a change of sex is pending. From level 38 each media entry has `crop`: the GEDCOM 7 crop (`2 CROP`) of this link as `{top, left, height, width}` in pixels (a missing value is `null`), else `null` – the part of the image that shows this individual. From level 39 a `thumb` (of this individual and of everyone in the answers that carry one) shows that part when the link to the main photo has a crop – see `Portrait`.

parameters.name: relativeTo
parameters.description: Relationship relative to this individual (default: own individual)

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

get.summary: Place suggestions while typing, like webtrees' own autocomplete.
get.description: Place suggestions while typing, like webtrees' own autocomplete. `Berlin, Deu` searches per level. With `list=1` (level 21, visitor): every place at a visible fact – as written there – with the number of events, individuals and families, coordinates and their origin (`location`: the GEDCOM-L `_LOC` record, `mapData`: webtrees' geographic data, `event`: `MAP` at a fact), the `_LOC` record and its GOV identifier. From level 27 also `type` (the `_LOC` record's TYPE: farm, house, parish …; with several dated TYPE lines the last one) and, since 1.18.1, `govType` (the GOV type number from `2 _GOVTYPE`, GEDCOM-L: 24 farm, 87 mill, 55 village …) and places that exist only as a `_LOC` in the GEDCOM-L hierarchy (`1 _LOC @parent@`, e.g. a farm without recorded residents) with 0 events. From level 32 `unlinked`: events at the place without the pointer `3 _LOC` (other programs such as the Online-OFB farm list find the `_LOC` only through it).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Beginning or part of the place name

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

get.summary: One place: levels, sub-places one level down, coordinates with origin, the `_LOC` record (GOV identifier, coordinates, notes, sources, media) and the individuals and families with their events at this place (at most 1000 each).
get.description: One place: levels, sub-places one level down, coordinates with origin, the `_LOC` record (GOV identifier, coordinates, notes, sources, media) and the individuals and families with their events at this place (at most 1000 each). The `_LOC` record is found like the Ortsregister module does: `3 _LOC` at the events, the module's binding, its GOV identifier, the leaf name if unique on both sides. From level 27 the `_LOC` record also carries `type` (TYPE, the last of several dated ones), `govType` (`2 _GOVTYPE`, since 1.18.1), `parents` (the GEDCOM-L hierarchy `1 _LOC @parent@` with pointer type and date) and `events` (`1 EVEN` at the place: fire, rebuilding, change of ownership … with type, date, notes, sources); `children` are merged from webtrees' place table and the `_LOC` hierarchy, each with `location`, `type` and `govType`. A place that exists only as a `_LOC` in the hierarchy is answered with 0 events. From level 32 `unlinked`: events here without `3 _LOC`. `not-found` if neither a visible event nor a `_LOC` names the place.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The place as written at the event, e.g. `Kortau, Allenstein`

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.summary: Save a place's data in its GEDCOM-L `_LOC` record – created if there is none.
post.description: Save a place's data in its GEDCOM-L `_LOC` record – created if there is none. Only the parts named in the body are replaced; sources, media and unknown lines of the `_LOC` stay. If the leaf name is not unique in the tree, the events at the place get the pointer `3 _LOC @L1@` (`linked`: how many); with `linkEvents: true` (level 32) every event at the place without a pointer gets it. `mapData: true` also writes the coordinates to webtrees' geographic data (site administrators only) – webtrees' own maps read only those and `MAP` at the events.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{name, gov?, lat?, lng?, note?, media?, mapData?, postalCode?, region?, country?, shortName?, type?, govType?, parent?, linkEvents?}` – `lat`/`lng` together, `null` removes the coordinates; `media` replaces the linked media objects (upload new ones with route Media and the `_LOC` identifier). `type` (level 27) sets the `_LOC` record's TYPE – only the value of the latest TYPE line changes, its `_GOVTYPE`, date and sources and older dated TYPE lines stay (1.18.1), empty removes all TYPE lines –, `govType` (level 32) sets or (`null`) removes the GOV type number `2 _GOVTYPE` of the latest TYPE; without `govType` an existing one stays. `parent` the identifier of the superior `_LOC` (`1 _LOC @parent@`): from level 32 only the current political pointer changes (undated, else the latest open-ended one; its date and sources stay), earlier dated pointers and church/geographic ones stay, a new pointer gets `2 TYPE POLI`; `null` detaches only the current one (up to level 31 all pointers were replaced); with `parent` a place without events may be created (a farm without recorded residents). Answer: `{ok, xref, pending, linked, mapData}`, status 201 when the `_LOC` was created.

post.summary: Change title and type of a media object (first file: `2 TITL`, `2 FORM` / `3 TYPE`); everything else stays.
post.description: Change title and type of a media object (first file: `2 TITL`, `2 FORM` / `3 TYPE`); everything else stays.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{title?, type?}` – type one of photo, document, certificate, book, newspaper, card, map, tombstone, audio, video, electronic, film, fiche, magazine, manuscript, painting, other; empty removes it.

get.summary: One media object with its files and everyone linked to it – each visible individual with `factId` and `crop` of their link (GEDCOM 7 `2 CROP`, `{top, left, height, width}` in pixels, or `null`): who is marked where on a photo.
get.description: One media object with its files and everyone linked to it – each visible individual with `factId` and `crop` of their link (GEDCOM 7 `2 CROP`, `{top, left, height, width}` in pixels, or `null`): who is marked where on a photo. `canEdit` tells whether the user may change the media object.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.summary: Change the signed-in user's own display name, as under “My account” in the browser.
post.description: Change the signed-in user's own display name, as under “My account” in the browser. Username, email and password stay with the browser.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{realName}`. Answer: `{ok, realName}`.

post.summary: Set the start person.
post.description: Set the start person. Without `forTree` the signed-in user's own default individual (as under “My account”; an empty `xref` removes it), with `forTree: true` the family tree's default individual (managers only). Route Info names per tree `startXref` – the individual webtrees starts with for this user, if visible – and `treeDefaultXref`.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{xref, forTree?}`. Answer: `{ok, startXref, defaultXref, treeDefaultXref}`.

post.summary: Rename a place or merge it into another.
post.description: Rename a place or merge it into another. Every event at `from` gets `to`; places below move along (`Kortau, Allenstein` → `Kortau, Olsztyn`). If `to` already exists it is a merge: the two `_LOC` records become one (gaps filled, notes, sources and media appended, differing GOV identifier or coordinates reported in `conflicts`) and the `3 _LOC` pointers point to it. Events the user may not edit (locked, confidential) stay and are counted in `skipped`. With `preview: true` nothing changes. Without automatic acceptance the changes are pending as usual.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{from, to, preview?}`. Answer: `{ok, preview, from, to, merge, records, events, subPlaces, skipped, location: {from, to, conflicts}, pending?}`.

post.summary: Merge two individuals: `xref2` is absorbed into `xref1`.
post.description: Merge two individuals: `xref2` is absorbed into `xref1`. Everything that pointed to `xref2` (families, sources, notes, media, associations) points to `xref1` afterwards, duplicate links are dropped, `xref2` is deleted – as webtrees' own merge does. Which facts stay is up to the client (`keep1`, `keep2`, fact ids); links (FAMC, FAMS, OBJE) always stay from both. With `preview: true` nothing changes: the answer lists both persons, their facts with a suggestion (`keep`: all of the first, from the second only what the first does not have word for word; `same` marks identical facts, `link` the ones that always stay), the records that link to `xref2` and `suggestions` – further pairs that are probably the same person too (father, mother, spouses and children with the same name). Without `preview` the merge is done and remembered: `mergeId` is the handle for `MergeUndo`. Only managers of the tree, like in webtrees. Without automatic acceptance the changes are pending as usual.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{xref1, xref2, keep1?, keep2?, preview?}`. Answer (preview): `{ok, preview, person1, person2, facts1, facts2, links, suggestions}`; (merge): `{ok, preview, xref, removed, mergeId, records, pending}`.

post.summary: Take a merge back.
post.description: Take a merge back. webtrees keeps every change with the old and the new text; the module remembered which changes belong to the merge and replays the old texts in reverse order – the deleted individual comes back under its old identifier, links point to it again. Only if none of the records was changed since: otherwise `changed-since` with the records in `changed`, and nothing is changed. Pending changes of the merge are rejected instead. With `preview: true` only the check is done. Without automatic acceptance the undo is pending as usual.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{id, preview?}`. Answer: `{ok, preview, xref, removed, records, pending?}`.

get.summary: The merges of this tree, newest first: who merged whom into whom and when, how many records were changed, and whether the merge was undone (`undone`: time or `null`).
get.description: The merges of this tree, newest first: who merged whom into whom and when, how many records were changed, and whether the merge was undone (`undone`: time or `null`).

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.summary: Add or change a fact or event.
post.description: Add or change a fact or event. Unmentioned sub-lines (sources, media …) are kept when changing. From level 32 a new or changed place gets the GEDCOM-L pointer `3 _LOC @L1@` when it belongs to exactly one `_LOC` record (pointers at other events with this place, the Ortsregister binding, or the `_LOC` name along its hierarchy); the same for places in AddIndividual and Link.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{factId?, tag, value?, date?, place?, address?, note?, type?}` or `{factId?, gedcom: "1 BIRT\n2 DATE …"}`. `type` (level 20) sets the fact's TYPE; for MARR in webtrees' form (civil → CIVIL, religious → RELIGIOUS, PARTNERS, COMMON LAW). `address` (level 33) sets the address `2 ADDR` of the event (lines as `3 CONT`), empty removes it; facts return it as `address`.

post.summary: Write godparents, witnesses and other associates of a fact.
post.description: Write godparents, witnesses and other associates of a fact. `linked` replaces the linked individuals (`2 _ASSO` + `3 RELA`, written as webtrees does: `godparent`/`witness`; `other` needs `rela`); an individual already linked keeps its sub-lines (sources) and its RELA spelling when the role matches; `note` replaces its embedded note. `free` replaces people without a record, one line each as `2 _GODP` (godparents) or `2 _WITN` (witnesses) as in GEDCOM-L – old notes "Paten: …"/"Trauzeugen: …" on the fact are converted. `convertLevel1` moves the person's `1 ASSO` for individuals named in `linked` into the baptism. Parts not named stay. Answer: new `factId`.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{factId, linked?: [{xref, role: godparent|witness|other, rela?, note?}], free?: [{text, role: godparent|witness}], convertLevel1?}`

get.summary: The main photo of an individual as a square thumbnail of their crop (`2 CROP` at their link to it) – the image itself, not JSON.
get.description: The main photo of an individual as a square thumbnail of their crop (`2 CROP` at their link to it) – the image itself, not JSON. `thumb` points here whenever that link has a crop (not when webtrees adds a watermark for the user); `crop` in the address changes with the crop. Error `no-portrait` when there is no cropped main photo.

parameters.name: crop
parameters.description: Changes with the crop, so caches never show an old part

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.summary: Turn the image of a media object clockwise by 90°, 180° or 270° (`quarterTurns` 1–3).
post.description: Turn the image of a media object clockwise by 90°, 180° or 270° (`quarterTurns` 1–3). The file is overwritten with the turned image – GEDCOM has no rotation – and the crop (`2 CROP`) of every link to it turns along, so each marked frame stays on the same face; `turnedCrops` counts them. Needs the right to upload media. Errors `invalid-turns`, `not-an-image`, `upload-not-allowed`, `crop-locked` (a link with a crop the user may not change – nothing is turned).

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{quarterTurns: 1 | 2 | 3}`

post.summary: Set the crop of a media link (GEDCOM 7 `2 CROP`, pixels): the part of the image that shows this record – each linked individual can have their own part of the same image, the file stays unchanged.
post.description: Set the crop of a media link (GEDCOM 7 `2 CROP`, pixels): the part of the image that shows this record – each linked individual can have their own part of the same image, the file stays unchanged. Links the media object first if it is not linked yet; `crop: null` removes the crop. Errors `media-not-found`, `invalid-crop` (`top`/`left` integers ≥ 0, `height`/`width` integers ≥ 1), `fact-locked`.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{media, crop: {top, left, height, width} | null}`

get.summary: All research tasks of the tree – webtrees' own `_TODO` facts at individuals and families (text, date, user, note), as the module “Research tasks” writes and shows them – at records the user may see, by date.
get.description: All research tasks of the tree – webtrees' own `_TODO` facts at individuals and families (text, date, user, note), as the module “Research tasks” writes and shows them – at records the user may see, by date. `?open=1` only the ones due (date not in the future; webtrees treats a future date as a reminder). A task is done when it is deleted (`DeleteFact` with its `factId`).

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: `1`: only tasks whose date is not in the future

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.summary: Add or change a research task at an individual or family: `1 _TODO text` with `2 DATE` (today when missing), `2 _WT_USER` (the signed-in user when missing) and `2 NOTE`.
post.description: Add or change a research task at an individual or family: `1 _TODO text` with `2 DATE` (today when missing), `2 _WT_USER` (the signed-in user when missing) and `2 NOTE`. With `factId` the task is changed, without it created. The answer's `factId` is the new id. Delete (= done) with `DeleteFact`.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{factId?, text, date?, user?, note?}`. Answer: `{ok, xref, pending, factId}`.

post.summary: Reorder children (`children`, at a family), partnerships (`families`), names (`names`, at an individual) or media (`media`, both) – like the “Re-order” pages in webtrees, only the order of the lines changes.
post.description: Reorder children (`children`, at a family), partnerships (`families`), names (`names`, at an individual) or media (`media`, both) – like the “Re-order” pages in webtrees, only the order of the lines changes. `order` lists the identifiers (for names the fact ids) in the new order; what is not listed comes after. The answer's `order` is the resulting order.

200.description: Result – or an error object (`ok: false`, see `Error`)

post.x-body: `{type: children|families|names|media, order: [...]}`. Answer: `{ok, xref, pending, order}`.
